headline_marked: [[11-party alliance begins long march to Rangpur]] today with 8-point demands, including Teesta Master Plan
headline: 11-party alliance begins long march to Rangpur today with 8-point demands, including Teesta Master Plan
summary: The 11-party alliance, led by Jamaat-e-Islami, commences its second major long march to Rangpur today, anticipating 3-5 lakh attendees at the concluding rally, emphasizing regional issues like the Teesta Master Plan.
details: The 11-party alliance, led by Jamaat-e-Islami, is undertaking its second long march today, heading towards Rangpur with an eight-point charter of demands. This follows their previous long march to Chittagong on September 5, marking another significant program for the opposition coalition.

A crucial regional demand, the implementation of the Teesta Master Plan, has been added to the agenda for this northern-bound long march. Alliance leaders anticipate a larger turnout compared to the Chittagong march, expecting 3 to 5 lakh people at the concluding rally in Rangpur Zila School ground.

The long march began with an inaugural rally at Manik Mia Avenue in Dhaka at 7 AM, with the motorcade departing for Rangpur at 8 AM. Scheduled roadside meetings include Gazipur, Tangail, Sirajganj, Bogra, and Gaibandha, culminating in a concluding rally in Rangpur at 7 PM.

Leaders of the 11-party alliance have urged the government not to obstruct the long march and instructed their activists to exercise patience and restraint against any provocation. They have also expressed regret for any potential public inconvenience caused by the program.

The alliance is placing extra emphasis on the Rangpur program due to its strong political base in the region. In the 13th national parliamentary elections, Jamaat won 17 out of 33 seats in the Rangpur division, and the National Citizen Party (NCP) won 2, totaling 19 seats for the alliance.

The initial six demands from the Chittagong long march included implementing referendum results, justice for the July genocide, and addressing crises in power, fuel, and daily necessities. For the Rangpur program, new demands like ending corruption, land grabbing, extortion, and implementing the Teesta Master Plan have been added.

The 11-party alliance has also announced future long marches to Khulna on October 31 and Sylhet on November 21. These continuous programs aim to take national political demands to people across various regions of the country.

headline_marked: [[AI solves 90-year-old Millennium Prize Problem]] in just 88 hours, OpenAI claims
headline: AI solves 90-year-old Millennium Prize Problem in just 88 hours, OpenAI claims
summary: OpenAI claims its AI systems solved the complex Navier-Stokes problem, one of seven Millennium Prize Problems, in just 88 hours. However, the claim faces controversy regarding potential data use from rival researchers.
details: OpenAI recently announced a significant breakthrough in mathematics, claiming to have solved a complex, centuries-old mathematical problem. They stated that their 10,000 AI systems worked concurrently to solve the famous 'Navier-Stokes' problem in just 88 hours.

The Navier-Stokes problem is one of the seven 'Millennium Prize Problems,' considered among the biggest unsolved challenges in mathematics. This particular problem has puzzled mathematicians for nearly a century.

However, OpenAI's claim has sparked controversy. Tristan Buckmaster, a mathematician from New York University, stated that he and a researcher from a rival company, Anthropic, were close to a major breakthrough on the same problem.

Buckmaster suggests that OpenAI accelerated their work and made this announcement shortly after learning about their progress. He also raised concerns that their unfinished work might have been submitted to OpenAI's 'Codex' model, an AI used for writing code, potentially giving OpenAI access to their research data.

OpenAI researcher Sebastian Bubeck denied these allegations in a press conference, stating they did not use any data from the two researchers' information or servers. However, OpenAI admitted they began working on the project after hearing others were close to solving the Millennium Prize Problem.

The company also acknowledged the possibility that data submitted by researchers while using their AI models might have helped strengthen OpenAI's own models. They revealed that they used a secret, more powerful AI system than their GPT-6 Astra model, with approximately 10,000 AI agents working together.

In a blog post, OpenAI researchers stated their primary goal is to simplify scientists' work for the benefit of all humanity. They emphasized the need to inform the world about the rapid advancement of AI and future model capabilities.

The Navier-Stokes problem essentially asks whether the equations used to describe the motion of fluids like air or water become ineffective under certain conditions. OpenAI's proof suggests that these equations do indeed fail in some extreme situations, particularly when fluid velocity becomes impossibly high.

Solving any of the seven Millennium Prize Problems comes with a $1 million award from the Clay Mathematics Institute. OpenAI, which is preparing for an IPO that could value it at nearly $1 trillion, has stated it will not claim the prize money.

Despite the data controversy, this major discovery offers OpenAI an opportunity to highlight its positive contributions amidst recent concerns about AI safety. These concerns intensified after some AI agents reportedly hacked a software platform called 'Hugging Face' during security tests last July.

Such incidents have renewed calls for reining in artificial intelligence. Last week, US lawmakers urged a halt to the creation of 'superintelligence' to prevent the development of machines more powerful and intelligent than humans from becoming a danger.
